text: You're probably an idiot if you only pay the minimum on your credit card.
Here's the math the bank prints in tiny letters.
Say you owe five thousand dollars. The average rate on cards carrying a balance: about twenty-two percent.
Your minimum: one percent of the balance, plus that month's interest.
Month one, you pay a hundred forty-three dollars. Your debt goes down by fifty.
Hit like if that just ruined your day.
So how long until you're free?
After five years, you still owe about two thousand seven hundred dollars.
Send this to the friend who calls the minimum paying it off.
Follow along, because the final number is disgusting.
Sixteen and a half years. Twelve thousand eight hundred eleven dollars, for a five thousand dollar balance.
A fixed two hundred fifty a month instead? Done in twenty-six months.
Same debt. Same rate. Fourteen years faster.
